today_summary: GCM26 marked $4,162.2 with ATM IV 21.30%, a $55.8 (1.34%) 1σ daily move. Top put walls sit at $3,500 (6,456 OI), $4,000 (4,620) and $3,900 (4,070); top call walls at $5,000 (12,101), $4,500 (10,192) and $4,725 (9,556) — P/C OI 0.39 on 237,042 calls against 93,306 puts. Net GEX within ±$200 of spot is −231.3 and the gamma flip strike sits $688 higher at $4,850, so the entire tradeable range is short-gamma. Session flow was one far-OTM bet: 3,007 contracts in the $5,100 call, 30% of the day's 9,890 call volume.
five_day_thesis: Spot round-tripped the week — +$34.0 from $4,168.3 into a $4,202.2 high on 10/02, then −$40.0 in a single session back to $4,162.2, netting −$6.1 and leaving a failed breakout rather than a trend. The decisive change is gamma: broad-window net GEX collapsed from +203.6 to +78.7 (−61%) in one session, while the ±$200 ATM window has been negative all five days (−237.9 → −231.3), so the stabilizing cushion that absorbed last week's drift is thinning around an already short-gamma core. Supply migrated up and away: the dominant call wall moved $4,500 → $5,000 as near-money $4,500 call OI bled 11,960 → 10,192 (−1,768) and $5,000 built to 12,101, removing the overhead pin that capped the 10/02 push. Downside conviction built quietly underneath — the $3,500 put wall held all five sessions and grew 5,300 → 6,456 OI (+22%). Yet short-dated hedging evaporated: put volume fell 11,036 → 2,123 (−81%) and ATM IV compressed 22.03% → 21.30% (−0.73pp), leaving the book cheaply hedged into a gamma regime that amplifies rather than dampens.

prediction: Bias bearish below $4,200.
